about: ACE-Step 1.5 cue spec, metal-v2 round: every recorded cue is a text-to-music take of distorted-guitar battle metal (levels), symphonic metal (intros, outros, menu), a battle-metal military march (clears, victory, finale) or a sinister alien march, generated at the cue's exact tempo (half-tempo conditioning, see `bpm_param`) and cut on its own downbeats. Takes are chosen by tempo (gate), loop seam, distorted-guitar and drum timbre (metal_metrics) and distance from the synth motif guide; a level's four tiers are picked jointly so their density rises. The fleet variants re-perform the chosen normal march audio-to-audio (same bars, bigger arrangement); the cackle re-performs the formant laugh. Prompts describe genre traits only; they never name a song, band, game or composer.

kinds.loop: whole file loops; length = beats exactly; the first crossfade_s blend the continuation into the start so the wrap is continuous
kinds.tail: plays `beats` once, then the appended copy of its last bar loops (loopStart..loopEnd) until the next cue
kinds.oneshot: plays `beats` once and ends with a fade over `fade_s`
kinds.sprite: accent sprite: one slot of `slot_beats` per accent (dive, laststand, hatch, reinforce), played on demand

tempo_note: ACE-Step 1.5 text-to-music asked for 150-180 BPM mostly settles near 140-150 BPM; asked for half the tempo in the BPM field (bpm_param) with the real tempo in the tags it locks to the real tempo (L1, 8 seeds: 7 at 170.0 BPM, drift <= 2.5 ms). `analyze` rejects takes whose lattice tempo is more than 0.4 % off; the rest are resampled to the exact grid.
method_note: Round 3 re-performed synthesized motif guides audio-to-audio at denoise 0.45-0.55, which kept the synth's tonal timbre (1-5 kHz flatness 0.09 against 0.26-0.47 for ACE's own metal takes). Higher denoise (0.6-0.9) and the base model with a negative prompt did not fix it: above 0.55 the takes lose the guide's rhythm (onset correlation < 0.15) and fall onto foreign pulses, and the timbre reference imposes a 0.4 s (150 BPM) pulse at any setting. Metal-v2 therefore drops the motif guide from the recorded cues (the motifs remain the MIDI fallback, the accents and the yardstick of `guide_distance`).
